title: The Empty Ship
subtitle: It returned as scheduled, yet empty-handed.

items.text: The Empty Ship

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Now we are listening to the new year collection …

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: ... The world-famous painting Mona Lisa was found and returned to Musée de Louvre in the afternoon of December 13th.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: ... The U.S. Congress passed the Federal Reserve Act on December 23rd, formally establishing the Federal Reserve System.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: ... The conflict between Austria-Hungary and Serbia has escalated. Bulgaria challenged the Bucharest Peace Treaty. Tension is building up over the Balkan Peninsula ...

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: ... In London, futurists gathered under Big Ben, celebrating the upcoming 1914 ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This is ... news of the outside world?
Sonetto puts Ms. Radio to her ears, paying full attention to the unfamiliar news.
After the snatches of news, when the channel knob has been turned to the right end, a familiar voice comes out.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What about on your side?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Well, I am with Sophia.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Arcana is still in the hall. She hasn't taken any action so far ... Got it.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Please keep an eye on the Manus followers. Be mindful of the restriction set by the bangle.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Who are you talking to?
Sonetto immediately hides Ms. Radio behind her.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Just checking up on Lilya.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Please stay vigilant during the patrol.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: This is the last place we need to check.
On the white, soft beach, there are several geometrical bodies in different shapes. Some have sunk deep in the sand, while others are still standing unyieldingly.
Just like a minimalist art exhibition.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: We must keep this graveyard clean. Our dead deserve to be left in peace and undisturbed by the phenomenal world.
Sophia gets down on one knee before a cone-shaped body, dusting it meticulously.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Sophia, you said this is the graveyard?
Her hand quivers a little.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Yes, the Geometry Graveyard, it is called.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Four years ago, my father was restored to a geometric body on his way back to the island. So was 37's mother, who was also on that ship.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hmm, why are you crying, Sophia?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I was wrong! We calculated it wrong! 37!!!

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: We miscalculated the impacted area of the Emanation. We thought the ships would be safe in the Gorgon Current, but the safe area is in fact five degrees away.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: When the Emanation happened, the bow of their ship had just entered the safe area. But it was too late ...

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: My dad is gone, so is your mom.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I know, but why are you crying?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: My mom and your dad have come back to us, right?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Have come back?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Do you call this ... coming back?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Like this? In the form of geometric bodies, cold and silent, being pushed to the shore?
37 frowns, looking confused.
But then, the corners of her lips turn up.
As usual, she works out the answer within seconds.
Swift and precise.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No. They have gone somewhere further.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Look at them. These geometric bodies, how pure and how elegant.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I've never seen such perfect geometric bodies before.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: If they are not from the eternal and transcendental world of Forms, how should we explain this?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I'm going to study the Emanation, Sophia.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This is the best chance ever. The transcendental world finally opens its door to us.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: We will reach our hands to the Forms and explore the oldest and eternal laws.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Will you help me, Sophia?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Next time ... next time, I will definitely make a better calculation, I promise.
Waves lap against the beach.
In the fine sand, the geometrical shapes are bathed unyieldingly in the moonlight. Despite the endless tides they maintain their form, never eroded nor washed away by time.
An eternal monument.
Sophia lowers her head, as if she is trying to cut herself out of a miserable memory.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Thank you for assisting 37 with her research, Sonetto.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hmm? No, I didn't do anything. Timekeeper knows the "Storm" better.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: You have helped us greatly by just coming onto this island.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: For all this time, 37 has been locked up in the laboratory, refusing to talk to anyone, nor participate in any group study.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Since the two-day Emanation in 1929.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: It is you who helped her revive her interest in other affairs in Apeiron.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: These are Timekeeper's contributions. I barely did anything.
Sophia smiles bitterly and looks away.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: ... I can't help 37.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Because I don't see the charm of numbers. I lack the perception that an integer should have.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: That's why I can't see my own number.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The numbers' ... charm?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Sorry, I have never thought about these. For me, arcanum is my inborn mission.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: If you ask me, you are an unbelievably excellent arcanist.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You can flatten the ground, clean up the beach, and rectify errors ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You did it in an efficient and precise manner, which is already an advanced ritual.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Any students who have sworn to knowledge can do this easily.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: They aren't doing my job because they wish not to waste time on these trivial fragments of the phenomenal world.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Because they have seen the truth.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The phenomenal world is never complete, like you can never draw a perfect circle there.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No matter how much time you spend on it or how sophisticated your device is, it is impossible to draw a perfect circle in the phenomenal world.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Errors always exist. The floating points after the decimal can be reduced, but not destroyed.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The perfect circle only exists in the abstract transcendental world.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Of course, anyone in the world can find out the value of Pi through the most primitive method.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Egyptians, Greeks, Chinese, and Babylonians, they have all tried. They made circles with twine, painted on the ground with twigs, or measured the land with cubit rods, but none of them actually drew a perfect circle.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: However different their practices were, they found out the sole truth—the approximate value of Pi.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Because the essence of the circle is hiding in the imperfect manifestation of it.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This is the truth. It is eternal, unchanged, pure, and transcendent.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Anyone can reach out to it at any time, in any place, by any means, and everyone will get the same answer from it.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The Forms transcend all Matters.
Her gaze is firm but distant.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The world of Matters we live in is being flooded and destroyed by the tides of pneuma. When the tides recede, what is left on the beach is the essence.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Err, this doesn't sound right.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Let me think. How come your theory reminds me of the Manus doctrine?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: 37, we see the "Storm" very differently.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Among all the other things, we saw it, first of all, as a disaster.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But earthquakes, floods, volcanic eruptions … these are also "disasters."

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: These catastrophic events happen not because they have a reason to destroy. They just happened in this world, like we do.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This is what my mother taught me. She must be proud that she's a perfect geometric body now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm sorry for mentioning your mother.
37 frowns.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Why do you apologize, Vertin? Are you feeling guilty?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This is a very unusual feeling for a number like you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I don't get it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Why did you say my number is 0?
TO BE CONTINUED…
